intro.heading: Markets exist because people need somewhere to exchange value, risk, and opportunity.
intro.body: One side wants in. One side wants out. One side wants protection. One side wants profit. No exchange = no market. And no market = no movement. This is why price moves at all.
intro.dayliNote: A market is just a meeting place for decisions. Buyers say "I'll pay this," sellers say "I want that," and price moves until both sides meet — that negotiation is what prints the chart.

tapCards.prompt: A quiet overnight session has almost no orders coming in. What do you expect price to do?

options.label: Stay muted — fewer buyers and sellers means less to print onto the chart
options.feedback: Right — no exchange happening means no real negotiation to move price.

options.label: Move just as much as any busy session
options.feedback: Participation and movement are linked — fewer participants means less real price discovery.

tapCards.prompt: Then New York opens and volume floods in. What changes?

options.label: Far more negotiation is happening — price has more real information to print
options.feedback: Exactly — more buyers and sellers meeting means more genuine disagreement getting resolved.

options.label: Nothing — volume doesn't affect how meaningful a move is
options.feedback: Volume is a real signal — a move on heavy participation reflects more real agreement/disagreement.

tapCards.prompt: A level gets tested twice — once overnight on thin volume, once at the New York open on heavy volume. Which test tells you more?

options.label: The New York open test — more participants means more real information
options.feedback: Right — not all tests of a level are equal. The one with more real participation carries more weight.

options.label: They're identical — a test is a test
options.feedback: They're not identical. Who showed up to make that test happen matters.

quiz.question: A slow, quiet holiday session has almost no participants placing orders. What would you expect to happen to price movement, and why?
options: It would likely stay muted — with fewer buyers and sellers meeting, there's less negotiation to print onto the chart
It would move just as much as any other session — participation doesn't affect movement
It would move randomly, unrelated to how many people are trading
quiz.explanation: Fewer participants means less real negotiation happening, so there's less to push price anywhere.

quiz.question: Why can't price move at all if literally no one wants to buy or sell?
options: Because someone has to want in and someone has to want out for a trade — and a new print — to happen
Price always moves regardless of participation
Price only moves when the exchange forces it to
quiz.explanation: Price only moves because buyers and sellers are actively negotiating. Zero participants means zero disagreement to resolve into price.

quiz.question: If nobody wants to buy or sell, price has no reason to:
quiz.explanation: No exchange happening means nothing is pushing price in any direction.
